title: US Supreme Court allows execution of Christa Pike to go ahead
description: Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, a conservative, granted Wednesday evening's application to vacate the stay of the execution. No explanation was
body: Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh, a conservative, granted Wednesday evening's application to vacate the stay of the execution. No explanation was provided in the order.The top court's three liberal justices - Sonia Sotomayor, Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson - dissented.Sotomayor wrote that the decision cleared the way for Tennessee to execute Pike before her pending legal challenges to her conviction "can be properly considered"."Tennessee's desire to expedite Pike's execution by a few days or even weeks cannot outweigh her 'fundamental interest in [her] own life," she said.The latest Supreme Court ruling landed just before 18:00 local time. The state's order for the execution at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville was due to expire at midnight. If time runs out, the Tennessee Supreme Court would need to set a new execution date, the Associated Press news agency reports.In a ruling earlier on Wednesday, judges from the US Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit paused the execution saying they needed more time to consider the arguments in Pike's case. Pike's lawyers said that for years, the state of Tennessee had argued in court that she lied about being sexually abused as a child.But at a recent hearing about her execution method, the state said it did not dispute that she had suffered sexual abuse and rape.Pike's legal team asked the appeals court to send her motion back to the district court, arguing that if the federal courts had based their ruling on the state's earlier claim that she was lying, then the federal review was affected.It was the second time in as many days that the US Supreme Court gave the go-ahead for the convicted murderer's death by lethal injection. On Tuesday, the justices rejected a different appeal from Pike.Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request this week from the death row inmate.At the time of her incarceration, the 21-year-old was the youngest person on death row, according to the Tennessee Department of Corrections.Pike is now the only woman currently serving a sentence on Tennessee's death row.Since 1976, when the Supreme Court resumed the death penalty, only 18 women have been executed in the US, compared to 1,663 men. That's about 1% of all US executions.In her clemency petition, Pike said that she intended to beat Slemmer, not kill her, but that she was unable to "put the brakes on"."I was a mentally ill 18-year-old kid," she said in a statement. "It took me numerous years to even realise the gravity of what I'd done. Even more to accept how many lives I affected. I took the life of someone's child, sister, friend. It sickens me now to think I had the ability to commit such a crime."The murder in 1995 created a media frenzy in Knoxville, Tennessee, after Colleen was found with an inverted pentagram - a symbol that is associated with satanic groups - carved into her chest. Pike has denied carving the symbol herself.Prior to the killing, Pike had accused Colleen of insulting her and trying to steal her then-boyfriend. Two other residents at the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the murder before and after, and showed them a piece of Colleen's skull.

schema.headline: US Supreme Court allows execution of Christa Pike to go ahead

title: Energy bills are going up - here's what you can do about it
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Keeping yourself warm by wearing thick clothes, using blankets and having hot drinks can help reduce heating
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Keeping yourself warm by wearing thick clothes, using blankets and having hot drinks can help reduce heating billsUpdated 4 hours agoEnergy prices have now risen by nearly 4%, with forecasts of a much bigger jump to come in January.Regulator Ofgem's price cap affects about 20 million households in England, Scotland and Wales and sets a maximum price for each unit of gas and electricity.Forecasters have suggested a 16% increase is possible in January, due to high wholesale prices paid by suppliers as a result of the conflict in the Middle East.While that's beyond consumers' control, charities say the government should offer more support - beyond a VAT cut on electricity bills which takes effect on Thursday -  and households should reset for winter again.That includes reading the meter now, and taking other steps to keep a check on rising bills.1. Consider switching to a fixed rateThe energy regulator, Ofgem, is advising people to consider fixing - so that the price you are charged per unit of gas or electricity does not change every three months, although the total bill will still vary depending on how much energy you use.The trouble is that it is very difficult to work out whether a fixed deal is a good deal at the moment.Should energy prices rise sharply, then those who have fixed already have the certainty of what they will pay for each unit of energy. That price may well be lower than the forecast price in January.However, if events in the Gulf region settle down, and a peace deal in the Iran war  leads to lower international gas prices, then a longer-term fix might not seem such good value compared with the price cap.So consumer group Which? also recommends keeping an eye on any exit fees when picking a fixed deal. If variable prices fall below your fixed rate and you want to get out of it before the end of your agreement period, you may have to pay a hefty sum.Before you fix, consumer website MoneySavingExpert advises you look at all the deals available, not just what your own supplier is offering.2. Pay by direct debitOfgem says about five million people still pay their bill when it arrives every three months. For some that's because they do not want their supplier to estimate their usage in case they are overcharged. Taking regular meter readings, or having a smart meter, while paying by monthly direct debit solves that problem. Moreover, paying by direct debit costs less per unit than by so-called standard credit.You will usually - although not always - need to switch to direct debit if you want to take advantage of the fixed deals on offer.Customers on prepayment schemes  - usually people on low incomes struggling to pay bills - used to pay a higher rate than others, but now they pay slightly less than the capped direct debit variable rate.There are also a range of pricing schemes offering cheaper off-peak electricity, for example if you are charging an electric car overnight.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Changing habits when using household appliances can also help, for example reducing washing machine temperatures3. Check what financial support you can getThere are a range of ways people on low incomes can access support.This winter anyone on means-tested benefits will get £150 off their electricity bill. Your supplier will apply the discount automatically unless you are in Scotland, where you will need to contact your energy company to ask for the help.Some people will also be eligible for a Cold Weather Payment, external and most pensioners will receive the winter fuel payment, after political pressure forced the government to U-turn on its plan to restrict it to the poorest pensioners.Beyond that, most energy suppliers offer hardship grants for people struggling to pay their bills and the government's Fuel Direct Scheme, external can help you repay energy debt.You can get more advice from Ofgem, external, Citizens Advice, external, or your own energy supplier. Trade body Energy UK has a list of support schemes, external.People on low incomes may also be eligible for grants to help with insulating their homes, and there are local schemes offering grants for solar panels, heat pumps and the like.But if you are hunting around for grants, watch out for scams pretending to be official money-off schemes.4. Take another look at your energy useOnce the temperature outside starts to fall again, it is important to stay warm, especially for the very young, old, and those with health conditions or reduced mobility.  But there are plenty of ways you can keep bills lower without letting the temperature in your home fall below the recommended 18C minimum.You may already have hung thicker curtains and blocked the draughts over the last couple of winters, but do not forget to switch off radiators in rooms you are not using and wrap up.MoneySavingExpert advises to "heat the human not the home".Turning down the flow rate on a combi boiler can save you money as often the water is being heated higher than it needs to be.Batch cooking and using an air fryer or microwave rather than heating up the oven for a small item can save energy.Take shorter showers and wash clothes at 30C rather than 40C. Dry clothes outdoors if you can, rather than using a tumble dryer, or hang clothes indoors but ventilate well or use a dehumidifier to avoid damp.If you are thinking about moving home, or undertaking renovations, it is worth thinking through how to reduce bills. When it comes to white goods, look for energy-efficient appliances.

schema.headline: Energy bills are going up - here's what you can do about it

title: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel
description: At 05:40, the plane - which had briefly entered Jordanian airspace - looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for land
body: At 05:40, the plane - which had briefly entered Jordanian airspace - looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for landing.Less than an hour later, the plane returned to squawk 7700.Initial local media reports cited Israeli officials as saying a fight had broken out between two pilots.But, speaking on Wednesday following the incident, Netanyahu confirmed later reports that one pilot had stabbed the other before "apparently trying to crash" the plane. He said an Israeli passenger told him "the plane went into a spin and began to descend" before the passenger and a crew member broke into the cockpit and overpowered the "pilot who had carried out the stabbing".The plane was diverted to Tabuk Airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia and touched down at 06:58, according to location data.The stabbed pilot, who is in a stable condition according to the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia, was later identified as Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar. Paying tribute to Machchhar, Netanyahu hailed him as a "true hero" and said "he saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals".Passenger Yaniv Hayun, who was later greeted and described as a hero by Netanyahu, said in a video released by the prime minister's office that he and others were trying to open the cockpit door, but the stabbed pilot was very close to it. Before the pilot collapsed, the injured man managed to open the door, Hayun said. He said that inside, the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane".Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside of the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down.He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane, explaining to Netanyahu that he watches Canadian documentary series Air Crash Investigation. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there."Zvika Meness, another passenger, told Israeli public broadcaster Kan News that he and other passengers tied the attacker up "with his own zip ties and with the multimedia headphones"."There are children and families here who have been through a very severe, highly traumatic event," he added.Yasmin Abukasis told Reuters that her daughter who was on the flight said a man holding a knife had forced one of the pilots onto the floor, with blood everywhere."The plane start to lose control. So all the people, they scream, they think they are going," Abukasis told AP news agency.Speaking from Ben Gurion Airport, she said her daughter phoned her to say she heard screaming as a pilot called for help, adding that two other pilots took control of the plane as other passengers ran towards a man who had a knife.Almog Itali, who was also on board the flight, told media that one of the pilots who landed the aircraft was British. The other pilot was European, Itali said, although he did not provide a specific nationality.One female passenger described the "very stressful" moment people realised the plane was descending. "We understood the pilots lost control," she told Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom."There are people here with shirts covered in blood," she said, adding: "Now we are fine and want to return home."Shortly after the incident, the Israeli and Saudi Arabian air forces dispatched fighter jets, while Netanyahu held urgent consultations.Speaking later on Wednesday, Netanyahu called the situation a "a very serious security incident".He added Israeli security forces are "maintaining close contact with the relevant authorities to ensure the continued safety of the passengers"."I salute these heroes who demonstrated extraordinary resourcefulness and courage," he added. "They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster."Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Machchhar's actions, calling him a hero on social media."His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy. India is proud of Captain Machchhar," Modi wrote in a statement posted on X.Flydubai meanwhile said "an altercation occurred in the flight deck" and the flight was "successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk airport".The airline said two replacement aircraft were sent to Tabuk to relieve the passengers and crew, and the incident had no impact on other scheduled operations. The repatriation flight carrying passengers left Tabuk at 17:40 local time (14:40 GMT) and arrived in Tel Aviv at around 18:40 local time (15:40 GMT). The spokesperson added: "Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved in this incident and support the official investigation."US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack.

schema.headline: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel

title: Japan raises permanent residency fees for foreign nationals by twenty-fold
description: Japan has raised fees for foreigners looking to reside in the country, with the cost of permanent residency going up 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270;
body: Japan has raised fees for foreigners looking to reside in the country, with the cost of permanent residency going up 20 times to 200,000 yen ($1,270; £955).Those seeking permanent residency must now also meet new income, pension and Japanese-language requirements.Long lines formed outside immigration offices earlier this week as applicants sought to beat the fee hikes, with Tokyo's main immigration bureau reporting wait times of over seven hours.The fee increases are part of a series of changes to Japan's immigration policy under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, which aim ito manage its rapidly growing foreign population.In July, Japan implemented a five-fold increase in visa fees for all foreigners – its first visa fee hike in 50 years. Authorities said this was meant to "reflect inflation and exchange rate fluctuations".Although immigration remains politically sensitive and restrictive in Japan, the nation's ageing population is increasingly relying on foreign workers to plug a labour shortage. Japan's foreign resident population surpassed 4.12 million at the end of 2025, marking a record 9.5% increase from the previous year. This however has led to growing anxieties over immigration and social change.Takaichi has made managing immigration one of her key priorities since she took office in October last year.In an X post days before the residency permit hikes set in, Takaichi wrote that her government recognises that "some members of the public may feel a sense of concern or unfairness" as Japan's foreign resident population grows."To address these concerns, [the government] is working to ensure that its policies toward foreign nationals are orderly, and that both Japanese citizens and foreign residents can live safely and securely," she wrote.Before the hikes, it would cost non-permanent residents in Japan 6,000 yen each time they applied to change their residency status or extend their period of stay.From 1 October, the fee varies according to the duration of stay sought – from 10,000 yen for three months or less, to 75,000 yen for five years or more.Applicants who face financial hardship or are designated as refugees would be granted discounts.Aspiring permanent residents must now also earn a stable income at or above the Japanese average. Latest data released in July puts average household income at 5.75 million yen as of 2024.Micaiah Michaela-Spence, who has been living and working in Tokyo for 10 years,  was not able to compile the necessary documentation to submit his application for permanent residency before the price hike. The 37-year-old still plans to apply, but questions the new measures aimed at foreign residents."My immediate reaction was that foreigners were being treated a bit too conveniently. We're being asked to make more than the average Japanese person, pay a significantly higher fee, just to be able to work in Japan and provide taxes," he tells the BBC."There's already a significant language and cultural barrier that prevents some talent from coming over. This just doesn't strike me as a plan that was thought out to the long term."From April next year, permanent residency applicants will face even tighter requirements, including basic Japanese language proficiency. This has led to a surge in enrollments at Japanese language schools as well as people signing up to take the Japanese-Language Proficiency Test, local media reported.Applicants' expected pension benefits must also be equivalent to that of someone who has enrolled into the employee pension system for 30 years, although the value of one's financial assets can be considered if their expected pension benefits fall short.

schema.headline: Japan raises permanent residency fees for foreign nationals by twenty-fold

title: Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss
description: Swiss glaciers have suffered a near-record loss of ice in 2026, new data shows, as intense summer heatwaves take their toll on Alpine peaks.More than
body: Swiss glaciers have suffered a near-record loss of ice in 2026, new data shows, as intense summer heatwaves take their toll on Alpine peaks.More than 5% of the country's remaining glacier ice has disappeared in the last 12 months, which scientists say is "extraordinary".They warn that such rapid melting is no longer a surprise given the pace of climate change, but it could threaten water supplies for farming, hydropower and transport in the decades ahead.The loss of glacier ice can also destabilise mountain slopes and increase the risk of landslides in some places - which can lead to flash flooding in extreme cases, as seen in Nepal in August.There were multiple factors involved in that event, which was triggered when a large area of bedrock and glacier ice collapsed. But scientists say long-term glacier thinning and the thawing of frozen ground likely raised the risks.The notable finding from this latest report is not so much that Swiss glaciers are shrinking - which is to be expected in our warming climate, driven primarily by fossil fuel emissions - but the sheer pace of melting. Until recently, glaciologists in the Alps considered 2% of ice lost in a single year to be "extreme". This year has seen an estimated 5.5% disappear."It's really just disastrous," said Dr Matthias Huss, director of Glacier Monitoring Switzerland, which produced the report.One of the most ominous findings is what researchers observed at measurement sites at the highest elevations, where temperatures are lowest and glaciers are typically snow-covered.Even as high as 3,500 metres above sea level, scientists found no snow remaining at the end of summer."At some glaciers we've seen four metres of ice loss at the highest point, where they should be covered by several metres of winter snow at this time of the year," said Huss, from Glacier Monitoring Switzerland.Snow is like glacier food - and under stable conditions some of it would eventually compact into ice.But if no snow survives the summer, it cannot replace the ice lost to melting at lower, warmer elevations. The glacier will starve, shrink and eventually disappear."Glaciers are complex because they gain mass at the top and they flow downstream, so there is a lot of physics," explained Maussion."But in its simplest form, what we see right now is that we took an ice cube out of the fridge and it's just melting in front of our eyes."Scientists say the climate is now too warm for many Alpine glaciers to survive.Some, like Plattalva in eastern Switzerland, have already disappeared.

schema.headline: Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss

title: Esther Rantzen: The story behind Nicholas Winton on That's Life!
description: Sir Nicholas was able to rescue the mainly Jewish cohort of children after briefly visiting Prague. He was knighted in 2003 for his humanitarian work.
body: Sir Nicholas was able to rescue the mainly Jewish cohort of children after briefly visiting Prague. He was knighted in 2003 for his humanitarian work.Sir Nicholas, who was born to German-Jewish parents, made a list of the children that needed sponsorship and found homes for them to go to in Britain.He worked alongside activists and humanitarians , externalin Czechoslovakia to navigate complex political obstacles, such as getting children to Britain through the Netherlands, which had closed its borders to Jewish refugees.Sir Nicholas was ultimately successful due to a House of Commons ruling on allowing young refugees in the country, which had been passed a couple of months before his rescue mission began.With the help of his mother, he put photos of the children in British magazines such as Picture Post to help find them homes and organised for hostels to take in some refugees too.He managed to raise money to cover travel for the children and provide them with essentials when they reached British soil.His incredible work went largely unreported for nearly 50 years - until his wife found a scrapbook in their loft, which contained names of children he had rescued.It was given to Holocaust researchers, who helped track down some of the children he had helped.Sir Nicholas' story became national news when he appeared on That's Life! in February 1988 and Dame Esther Rantzen told viewers about his story. Speaking in February 2024, Dame Esther said when she first got in touch with Sir Nicholas, who she called Nicky, she "congratulated him on his extraordinary achievement".She told The Radio Times, external he had expressed some disappointment about his efforts, commenting that "not enough" people had been saved."I was devastated that he felt he had failed. I wanted to prove to this extraordinary man that every life he had saved was precious," Dame Esther added.She invited him onto That's Life and during his first appearance, his scrapbook was shared with the audience, and two women he had saved as children - Vera Gissing and Lady Milena Grenfell-Baines - revealed their identities to him on TV.They were sitting either side of Sir Nicholas, who had no idea of the surprise - something Dame Esther recalled as "incredibly moving".Lady Milena is one of the most well-recognised Holocaust survivors in the UK.She left Prague with her younger sister Eva at the age of nine, travelling on a special train arranged by Winton. The two sisters were looked after by a Tameside family until their mother arrived the following year, having escaped via Norway.Gissing, who was rescued from Prague in 1939 at the age of 11, lost most of her family during the Holocaust and ended up settling in the UK after the war ended."That was the only time in my career when I had to stop recording to wipe away my tears," Dame Esther also said.The production team at That's Life were then contacted by several viewers who had watched the show and realised their connection to Sir Nicholas.That gave the show's team an idea which would go on to become one of British television's most famous moments."In our next episode, I asked all those who owed their lives to him to stand, and Nicky, whom we had seated on the front row, turned to see the whole ground floor of the Television Theatre on their feet," Dame Esther recalled.This is a TV moment many will remember and in subsequent years has been rediscovered by new audiences thanks to social media.Dame Esther said she watched the episode "many times" and "each time found myself deeply moved".She says she kept in contact with Sir Nicholas, meeting regularly until his death in 2015 at the age of 106.They would always have a connection due to the TV show, but Dame Esther said hearing the stories of the children he had saved also made her feel "immensely lucky" to have been a Jew born in England in the 1940s.Sir Nicholas' work has been the subject of a number of different films and documentaries, most recently the biopic One Life.Starring Sir Anthony Hopkins, the film premiered at the Toronto Film Festival and was released in the UK in January 2024.Dame Esther said it had been estimated "that 6, 000 people owe their very existence to Nicholas Winton".She added: "The Jewish children Nicky rescued were almost the only ones in Czechoslovakia to survive the Holocaust".And thanks to Dame Esther relaying his story to viewers on That's Life!, millions of people are now aware of the huge impact Sir Nicholas had.

schema.headline: Esther Rantzen: The story behind Nicholas Winton on That's Life!

title: BBC paying to air shows like Suits and Schitt's Creek is illogical, MPs say
description: The BBC should not pay "over the odds" for the rights to overseas hits such as Suits and Schitt's Creek, an influential group of MPs has said. It is o
body: The BBC should not pay "over the odds" for the rights to overseas hits such as Suits and Schitt's Creek, an influential group of MPs has said. It is one of several issues raised in a wide-ranging report about the BBC's funding and future, published by the House of Commons' cross-party culture and media committee.Although the BBC produces a lot of its own programmes, the corporation buys some international shows for its TV channels and iPlayer streaming platform.The MPs' report said the BBC could "spend more wisely when competing for programming". Overall, the BBC brings "immeasurable benefits" to society but needs reform of the TV licence fee to avoid a fate of "managed decline", they said.Committee chair Dame Caroline Dinenage said the report , externalcomes at "a pivotal moment for the BBC", which is grappling with changing media habits, declining income and negotiations with the government over how it is paid for.Dame Caroline said the government "must ensure the BBC has a universal and sustainable source of funding".But, she added, the BBC "can play its part by sweating its assets and boxing clever for the licence payer by ending illogical practices such as outbidding commercial rivals for overseas hits such as Suits, Schitt's Creek and Scooby Doo".The rights to air all three programmes were bought by the BBC after contracts with other networks or streaming services expired."At a time of constrained resources, the BBC should not be paying over the odds for overseas content, particularly when it's a bidding war against commercial UK broadcasters," the committee said.The MPs added that they "did not believe that this provides value for money for the licence fee payer".The BBC said it spends less than 5% of its content budget on acquiring shows, less than other broadcasters, and they are a cost-effective way of delivering high-quality content to audiences who go on to discover homegrown programming.The committee said there were "considerable challenges" for the BBC and warned that the current TV licence fee is "outdated and no longer fit for purpose".Currently, about 94% of individuals use the BBC each month but only 80% of households pay for a TV licence, the MPs noted."The licence fee should be reformed so it is no longer linked to the consumption of live TV or to a particular device, such as a television set," the committee said. "This should be an easier sell to licence fee payers if expanding the base is paired with a drop in the individual cost."The BBC's director-general Matt Brittin has previously described the current licence fee model as "a busted flush" and "yesterday's model", and has said the price could be cut if more people pay under an overhauled system.The committee also suggested the BBC should:Explore the opportunity for introducing an international TV licence so it can increase its revenue and global audienceWork with independent production companies who own the rights to many of its programmes to ensure more remain on iPlayerDevelop its current premises with facilities that can "harness the potential of new media and support the creator economy"The committee suggested the government should:Support the corporation by legislating to put a BBC button on remote controls for smart TVsPress YouTube to give a certain level of prominence for content made by the BBC and other British public service broadcastersTake back full funding for the BBC World Service, describing it as "the UK's number one soft power asset"The committee supported opening up BBC iPlayer to shows from other public service broadcasters such as Channel 4.Earlier this week, Channel 4 chief executive Priya Dogra said, external she was open to her network's content being hosted on iPlayer.The report also called for the end of political appointments to the BBC board, to improve governance and remain trusted by the public. And the committee recommended that the BBC is given new public purposes relating to innovation and technology and combating misinformation and disinformation.The BBC welcomed the report, which it said made "some important and interesting recommendations on the future of the BBC".A BBC spokesperson said: "We have consistently argued that the current funding model is outdated and needs reform, so we welcome the Committee's support for maintaining universal funding while overhauling the licence fee."We are also pleased to see their recognition of the vital work of the World Service, with a clear recommendation that responsibility for funding should return fully to Government."At a time of huge disruption in the media, the BBC's trust, reach and creative strength remain unparalleled. But we also recognise the need to evolve and move faster towards the future."The government's Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) said it "agrees entirely with the Committee's conclusion that it is in the country's best interests for the next Charter to support an ambitious and innovative BBC, and that the corporation cannot be left to a future of managed decline".A DCMS spokesperson added: "We will review and consider the committee's recommendations in detail, alongside the views of the public and other stakeholders, to inform decisions for the next Royal Charter."

schema.headline: BBC paying to air shows like Suits and Schitt's Creek is illogical, MPs say

title: Celebrity Traitors: What you need to know ahead of the first show
description: Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC CreativeImage caption, Maya Jama, Michael Sheen and Bella Ramsey are among this year's celebrity co
body: Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC CreativeImage caption, Maya Jama, Michael Sheen and Bella Ramsey are among this year's celebrity contestantsByHelen BushbyCulture reporterThe Celebrity Traitors is back for a second series, and viewers will see the likes of Michael Sheen, Jerry Hall, Richard E Grant and Amol Rajan at the round table along with Bella Ramsey, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Maya Jama and King Kenny. There are 21 celebrities taking part in total - two more than last year - and there will be an extra episode after the huge popularity of last year's series.The extended 75-minute debut episode starts at 20:00 BST on Thursday, with Claudia Winkleman again hosting the murderous game.Viewers can expect some fresh ideas, and executive producer Sarah Fay said they "always want to push the envelope" with the show's elaborate tasks."We're always trying to evolve existing ideas to bring them into a new life or coming up with different cultural references," she told the show's press launch.Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC CreativeImage caption, The Celebrity Traitors are finally gathered for episode one of series twoThe celebrities will be playing for a £100,000 cash prize for charity.The final amount will depend on how well they perform in the tasks, regardless of any possible tensions over who is a faithful and who is a traitor.This year's contestants are a mixture of famous faces from TV, film, radio and YouTube:Amol Rajan – journalist and broadcasterBella Ramsey – actorJames Acaster – comedian and podcasterJames Blunt – singer/songwriterJerry Hall – model and actressJoanne McNally – comedianJoe Lycett – comedianJulie Hesmondhalgh – actorKing Kenny – content creatorLeigh-Anne Pinnock – singer/songwriterMaya Jama – broadcaster and entrepreneurMichael Sheen – actor and presenterMiranda Hart – actor and authorMyha'la – actorProfessor Hannah Fry– broadcaster and mathematicianRichard E Grant – actor and authorRob Beckett – comedianRomesh Ranganathan – comedianRoss Kemp – actor and presenterSebastian Croft – musician and actorSharon Rooney – actorIn the show's trailer, external, they are seen arriving in a church, smiling as they greet each other, but looking nervous.They later travel to the castle in a fleet of black cars, before Winkleman chooses her traitors while everyone wears their blindfolds.They then take part in their first mission in a lake in wetsuits, ending with Winkleman saying ominously: "Fame won't save them."Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC CreativeImage caption, Romesh Ranganathan, Myha'la and Richard E Grant are also taking their places at the round tableSpeaking at the press launch, Winkleman said she is totally focused on the celebrities while she's in the castle, and is glued to the monitors showing footage of them throughout the day. "All of them were tremendous, and when we do any series I have this room with the monitors. I'm like a weirdo just applying fake tan, watching," she said. The presenter added that even when she's told to go home, she tells the producers "I am not leaving", joking that she got barely any sleep. Ed Gamble, host of BBC Two spin-off show Uncloaked, added that he watched "hours of footage a day" as well."So when they're eating breakfast, I'm eating breakfast watching them eat breakfast. It's actually quite sad... I'm normally sat there in my pyjamas eating cereal, watching them eat cereal," he told BBC News.Viewers can also look forward to more of Winkleman's eclectic wardrobe choices. "I like the fact that it is 'human crow meets golf caddy meets the Artful Dodger'. We're pretty happy with it," she joked about this year's outfits.Image source, BBC/Studio Lambert/Cody Burridge/BBC CreativeImage caption, Claudia Winkleman said her clothes are as distinctive as ever on the showThe celebrities have also been speaking about the show before its launch, with comedian and presenter Romesh Ranganathan saying that despite being best friends with fellow comic Rob Beckett, he would have no problem stabbing him in the back."I mean, he's just as easily going to be on my side as he is going to twist the knife in my back given the opportunity," he said.The show's other comics include Joe Lycett, James Acaster and Joanne McNally. "I think we're going to be the first ones under the magnifying glass being looked at," Acaster said over suspicions one will be a traitor.Comedian Alan Carr won the first series of Celebrity Traitors, which was the most watched TV programme of 2025 in the UK, watched by 15 million people.The Last of Us and Game of Thrones star Bella Ramsey already has experience of playing similar games at drama clubs and at home, which is why they joined the show."I've been playing a version of The Traitors since I was 10 years old," they said.Mathematician Hannah Fry, who called herself "toxically competitive", added she has already looked for "statistical patterns" in the data for previous games; while Little Mix singer Leigh-Anne Pinnock said she took advice from singer Cat Burns, who reached the final as a traitor last year."She had good advice. She said it might get intense around that round table – but remember, it's just a game," Pinnock said.'I wouldn't be a contestant'The show is also something of a love letter to the Scottish Highlands, where it is filmed, with sweeping drone shots of the scenery and Ardross Castle in Inverness, where the celebrities meet, eat and of course sit at the round table."It's breathtaking," Winkleman told the press, adding that she and her family were returning to the Highlands for a holiday."My husband was like, 'You're already there quite a lot, what's the matter with you?'" she said."It's the most beautiful place I've ever been in the world, is the truth."After she recently chose to end her recent BBC One chat show, Winkleman is back on familiar ground with Celebrity Traitors. BBC News asked if she would ever want to try being a contestant on the show, perhaps in the US or Australian versions."No, I'm too thick," she said in typical self-deprecating style."I mustn't play it in public. I must not."I'm just being honest - it's a privilege to play that game and to be at the round table, but I think I would just be too awful at it."The Celebrity Traitors series two begins on Thursday 1 October at 20:00 BST on BBC One and iPlayer. The series will air two nights a week, on Thursday and Friday evenings.

schema.headline: Celebrity Traitors: What you need to know ahead of the first show

title: 'Hero' pilot stabbed by other pilot on Israel-bound plane, Israeli PM says
description: Figure caption, ByHenry MooreUpdated 56 minutes agoA pilot has been arrested after he stabbed the other pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv and "
body: Figure caption, ByHenry MooreUpdated 56 minutes agoA pilot has been arrested after he stabbed the other pilot on a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv and "apparently tried to crash the plane", Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said.Passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control of the Flydubai aircraft, landing it safely at an airport in Tabuk, northwestern Saudi Arabia, with more than 170 people on board.The passengers, who were almost all Israeli, arrived later on Wednesday in Tel Aviv on a repatriation flight.The stabbed pilot, named as Indian national Captain Smit Machchhar, has been taken to hospital but is reported to be in a stable condition. Netanyahu and India's leader Narendra Modi praised him as a "hero"."Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back, resisted, opened the cockpit door, and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker — preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster," Netanyahu wrote on X."He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals."The Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar was in a stable condition in hospital.Modi praised the pilot's actions, writing on X: "In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others."India is proud of Captain Machchhar."Image source, EPAImage caption, Passengers arrived in Tel Aviv after their original flight was forced to land in Saudi ArabiaNo motive for the incident has been given and the pilot was under investigation in Saudi Arabia, Netanyahu told Fox News on Wednesday night, before he was expected to be taken back to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where the flight took off from.Israel was "likely" to contribute to the investigation, the prime minister added.US President Donald Trump said he had spoken with Netanyahu following the incident, saying it seemed as though the attacker was "perhaps a terrorist" or there were other reasons behind the attack.Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz has also called it an "attempted jihadist terror attack", without giving any details.Flydubai's flight FZ1073 took off from Dubai International Airport in the UAE at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time), en route to Ben-Gurion Airport in Israel.Around two and a half hours into its journey, data from flight tracking website Flightrader24 reported a rapid descent over Saudi Arabia, dropping more than 17,000 feet (over 5,000m) in less than two minutes.Minutes later, the plane signalled an emergency code - squawk 7700 - before switching it to a squawk 7500 code reporting a hijacking.Around 20 minutes after these codes were signalled, the plane looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent for landing.Less than an hour later, the plane returned to squawk 7700.Shortly after the incident, the Israeli and Saudi Arabian air forces dispatched fighter jets, while Netanyahu held urgent consultations.Initial media reports suggested a fight had broken out between the aircraft's two pilots, causing the rapid descent and landing.However, in the hours after the plane touched down in Tabuk, eyewitness accounts and a statement by Netanyahu confirmed one of the pilots had stabbed the other and, according to the Israeli prime minister, "apparently tried to crash" the aircraft.He said an Israeli passenger told him "the plane went into a spin and began to descend" before the passenger and a crew member entered the cockpit and overpowered the "pilot who had carried out the stabbing".Two on-duty crew travelling on the flight were then able to land the plane safely, Flydubai said.In an address on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu called the situation "a very serious security incident" and said Israeli security forces were "maintaining close contact with the relevant authorities to ensure the continued safety of the passengers".Unlike Israel's defence minister, Netanyahu did not give a motive for the incident."I salute these heroes who demonstrated extraordinary resourcefulness and courage," he added. "They saved many lives and prevented a major disaster."Image source, ReutersFlydubai said in a statement that "an altercation occurred in the flight deck" and the flight was "successfully secured by on-duty Flydubai crew travelling on the flight, who diverted and landed the aircraft safely at Tabuk airport".An airline spokesperson added: "Our immediate priority is to ensure the ongoing safety, health, and wellbeing of all passengers and crew members involved in this incident and support the official investigation."The passengers who had been on board flight FZ1073 arrived in Tel Aviv at around 18:40 local time (15:40 GMT). They were greeted at the airport by crowds of onlookers playing music, singing, dancing and waving Israeli flags.A number of people were "very emotional and crying as they came off the plane," a paramedic from Israel's ambulance service told the BBC.One passenger, Yaniv Hayun, met Netanyahu and told him how he and others on the flight had restrained the attacker."The pilot who was stabbed was simply very close to the door, so it was hard for us to open it," Hayun said in a video posted on social media by the prime minister's office, but before the stabbed pilot - now identified as Machchhar - collapsed, he was able to open the door. Yaniv said he put the attacker, who was trying to disable the plane, in a chokehold before other passengers helped pin him down.He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane and after it levelled out, another pilot took over control. Figure caption, Zvika Meness, another passenger, told Israeli public broadcaster Kan News that he and other passengers tied the attacker up "with his own zip ties and with the multimedia headphones".He said: "There are children and families here who have been through a very severe, highly traumatic event."

schema.headline: 'Hero' pilot stabbed by other pilot on Israel-bound plane, Israeli PM says

title: Vape tax comes into force with prices set to rise
description: Vape prices to rise as new tax takes effectImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The government is trying to make vaping more expensive and less ap
body: Vape prices to rise as new tax takes effectImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, The government is trying to make vaping more expensive and less appealing to young peopleByEmer MoreauBusiness reporterThe price of vapes is set to rise as a new tax comes into effect, with the aim of making vaping less attractive to children and young people.The Vaping Product Duty will be imposed at a rate of £2.20 per 10ml of e-liquid. However, many customers will not see a jump in prices immediately, as sellers have six months to sell old stock at the pre-duty price.The government wants to reduce the appeal of vapes by making them more expensive, as more evidence of its adverse effect on health comes out, particularly on children and young people.The vaping industry has lobbied against the new tax, saying that affordable vapes help people to quit smoking.The duty will apply to all vaping products regardless of whether they contain nicotine.Tobacco rates were also raised on Thursday, by £2.20 per 100 cigarettes or 50g of tobacco. HMRC said this maintains the financial incentive for smokers to switch to vaping.Stocking up v cutting downThe BBC spoke to vapers in Reading who had mixed views on whether the new tax would encourage people to quit.Mackenzie Bird, 19, has been a regular vaper for three years. She said she was "fine" with the duty and it wouldn't stop her from vaping.Image caption, Mackenzie Bird said the tax wouldn't stop her from vaping"I don't know how many people it'll actually deter," she said."I'll probably just stock up."However, Cara Lewis-Rimes and Dylan Killner said they might reconsider the habit in light of higher prices.Cara said she thinks the changes will force vapers to cut down because of the cost of living.Image caption, Cara and Dylan think the tax will prompt vapers to cut backDylan said he might be inclined to quit altogether."I don't think it's doing me any favours... the health factor around it as well is not great."Fighting illegal tradeHMRC is also launching a stamp for vaping products which are traceable throughout the supply chain.All vapes sold in the UK must carry this stamp from April.The new tax is also an effort to combat illicit trade, which is a growing problem on UK high streets. Last month, the prime minister announced new powers for councils that will address the decline of the high street, including the amount of vape shops.Changes to planning law in England mean every new shop selling e-cigarettes, or vapes, would need to apply to their local council for permission to open.Health Minister Karin Smyth said: "These measures are an important step in our ambition to tackle youth vaping by reducing the affordability of vaping products, which goes hand-in-hand with the work we are already doing to tackle the appeal and availability of vapes on our high streets."James Murray, the Financial Secretary to the Treasury, said the government was "backing all those retailers who play by the rules".Image caption, Vape shop staff like Jordan have seen customers stocking up ahead of the tax coming inBut Jordan Apap, a sales assistant in Berkshire Vapers, said the new tax would "put a lot of strain on legitimate vape shops" that provide more specialist advice and services than convenience stores and phone shops that sell vapes."There is a real and genuine risk that we will cease to exist within a year or two," he said.John Dunne, the director general of the UK Vaping Industry Association, said: "This is nothing short of a tax on public health."He said vapes had helped "millions of adults cut down on or stop smoking"."Protecting young people is essential. But that means stronger enforcement against illegal and rogue traders, not making legal vaping more expensive for adults trying to stay away from cigarettes."Experts say vaping is much safer than smoking, but it is not risk free and the long-term effects are less clear.A recent review of vaping studies found that it had an association with problems in children and young people including wheezing and coughing, poor oral and dental health, poor sleep, mental health problems and eye symptoms.The NHS has said that children and non-smokers should never vape.Additional reporting by Neranjana Elapatha

schema.headline: Vape tax comes into force with prices set to rise

title: Brendan Venter: Saracens' 'wine consultant' misses another press conference
description: Saracens head coach Joe Shaw has refused to say when, or if, director of rugby Brendan Venter will speak to the media again, despite the club facing f
body: Saracens head coach Joe Shaw has refused to say when, or if, director of rugby Brendan Venter will speak to the media again, despite the club facing fines for him not doing so.Venter was not at Wednesday's pre-match press conference for their forthcoming game with Sale after not attending Prem Rugby's pre-season launch day, or doing any media duties before, during or after the opening-weekend victory at Leicester.The Daily Telegraph reported on Tuesday that Venter had "resigned" as director of rugby and taken up a new role as "head of rugby culture and wine consultant", but this has not been confirmed by the club nor Prem Rugby.When asked if Venter would resume media duties, as part of his responsibilities as a director of rugby, Shaw said: "I'm just going to talk about the rugby. "I'll leave the club to talk about where we stand on all those kind of things."BBC Sport has contacted Saracens for comment.It is understood Sarries have already been fined £5,000 after Venter was not present at the Prem's pre-season launch day.It is also thought a change of job title would not preclude Venter from his contractual responsibilities.Saracens announced in January that Venter would be returning as director of rugby and have yet to publicly confirm any change to his day-to-day responsibilities.He succeeded Mark McCall, who stepped down at the end of last season after 15 years in the job.

schema.headline: Brendan Venter: Saracens' 'wine consultant' misses another press conference

title: Manchester City charges: Punishment before end of season, Premier League clubs believe
description: Manchester City's punishment for breaching Premier League rules should be handed down before the end of this season, senior football figures have told
body: Manchester City's punishment for breaching Premier League rules should be handed down before the end of this season, senior football figures have told BBC Sport.The Premier League said on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of its financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.They included artificially inflating revenue by more than £900m through "sham" sponsorship deals.City have repeatedly denied guilt and signalled an intent to lodge an appeal by the end of this week.There have been fears that the process, which has taken three years since City were charged, could be drawn out for much longer.However, senior figures within football have told BBC Sport they see no reason why the case cannot be concluded by the end of this season.Speaking on condition of anonymity, one club official said: "It benefits everyone for this to be resolved as quickly as possible."When asked if they believed it would be, they said: "Instinctively yes, but it has to be done right."We can all see what the risks are if it's not. But those risks have been there throughout the process, as they've won the league multiple times during it."Another source said the process  "should" be resolved by the end of the season, and they hoped any appeal would be "compressed".The final decision rests in the hands of the independent commission, with the Premier League board - and City - able to suggest a suitable punishment before the panel makes its decision.There is increasingly a desire to have the case resolved by the end of the season amid fears that allowing City to get to the end of the campaign without punishment could lead to uncertainty and farce, particularly if they were to win the title.One section of the Premier League regulations says an appeal should conclude no more than 12 weeks after it is filed, and a decision should be made within 30 days of its end.Procedures can be hurried to meet certain deadlines, like the end of a league season.However, Ferran Soriano, the club's chief executive, has suggested the case will run for a long time.Manchester City cannot make a further appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), but could potentially claim the process was not impartial at the High Court.The Premier League's statement, formally announcing the guilty verdicts read on Monday, said it wants the process to be "concluded as soon as possible".Meanwhile, City club sponsor Etihad Airways said it is considering legal action against the Premier League. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the United Arab Emirates-based airline said it "categorically rejects any finding, conclusion or implication that suggests the airline has ever been involved in improper commercial arrangements".It added: "The Premier League's public communication of the commission's findings, following a period of selective leaks and reporting, has further created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the redacted published findings."Etihad, City's main sponsor since 2009, also said it was given no opportunity to engage in a process that now reflects "adversely on the airline".The statement added: "Etihad is deeply concerned by the way this matter has been communicated publicly. "The lack of clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad despite the airline not being named in the published decision. "The Premier League must take responsibility for the consequences of the way in which these findings have been presented."Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests."The Premier League declined to comment when contacted by BBC Sport.

schema.headline: Manchester City charges: Punishment before end of season, Premier League clubs believe

title: Fury vs Joshua: Heavyweights trade jokes at launch event
description: After more than a decade of public feuding and false starts, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua exchanged pleasantries, traded jokes and even discussed goi
body: After more than a decade of public feuding and false starts, Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua exchanged pleasantries, traded jokes and even discussed going for a pint at a news conference in London.The British heavyweight rivals will fight at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December.But for all the history between them, the launch felt more like two veterans in the closing stages of long, turbulent careers taking stock of how far they had both come."He's been a role model and poster boy for British boxing for years," Fury, 38, said of Joshua. "I mostly find myself defending my arch rival to fans in the street."On Monday, there was still uncertainty over whether the fight would happen because of contractual disagreements surrounding the promotion.There had been plenty of reason to expect fireworks on Wednesday. Instead, Joshua, 36, spoke about the magnitude of the event."It's breathtaking and I'm not saying that lightly," he said. "I'm really grateful for this opportunity and bringing it to Great Britain because I know people in pubs have had proper fights about who will win and family members have fallen out."The mood was perhaps best summed up at the face-off, when Joshua smiled and pretended to tickle Fury's stomach.There was something almost surreal about seeing Fury and Joshua finally sitting side by side after so many years in which their rivalry had existed mostly through interviews, social media and failed negotiations.Both had arrived hours earlier for one-to-one interviews. When the news conference began, master of ceremonies Michael Buffer introduced the pair as fireworks shot up from the front of the stage.They entered from opposite sides at the same time - Joshua relaxed and composed in a grey tracksuit and sunglasses, Fury in more flamboyant fashion in a vivid emerald-green suit covered in crown motifs over a white shirt.Alongside the world's media, a few hundred fans filled the balcony above and quickly made their allegiance known as "Oh Anthony Joshua" rang around the British Airways ARC.Joshua has been credited with pushing to keep the fight in Britain and, if Wednesday was any indication, can expect strong backing in Cardiff - even with the main event potentially starting about 02:00 GMT to suit American audiences.For two men whose names have been linked for so long, Fury and Joshua have spent remarkably little time together. But their famous sparring session in 2010, when Joshua was still an amateur, soon became the topic of conversation.Fury suggested he had got the better of it, prompting one fan to shout: "Liar." Joshua smiled and said he could not remember.For those who believe the fight has come years too late, Fury had a simple response. "It's the icing on the cake of two great careers," he said. Moments later, he glanced back at the word "Finally" on the giant screen behind them.There were several moments of common ground. Fury nodded along as Joshua spoke about his Christian faith and, even when the pair traded insults, they rarely felt venomous."This man here is carved in stone and every time he gets cracked on the jaw, he falls over," Fury said."When I crack him on the jaw with a big right hand, he's going down."Joshua laughed and shouted back Fury's own catchphrase: "Get up."The fight has been reported as being for the vacant WBA 'super' heavyweight title, although current WBA heavyweight champion Murat Gassiev's team has lodged a formal objection over the proposed title arrangement.For a moment, it appeared the mood could turn when Joshua revealed he had received a call asking whether Fury's name could appear first in the promotion."You've been crying behind the scenes to get out of this fight. I've checkmated you. You have to fight," Fury replied."I've actually never won a world title here. Now it's on the line, we can become a three-time."That exchange came after several chaotic days in which the role of UFC and Zuffa Boxing chief Dana White had threatened to overshadow the fight.Netflix had presented White as part of the promotion alongside Turki Alalshikh's The Ring, despite Joshua promoter Eddie Hearn insisting his fighter's contract prevented White from having a promotional role.But White did not attend Wednesday's launch. And when Alalshikh thanked the American from the stage, his name was met with jeers from sections of the crowd.Fury did momentarily take aim at Hearn, calling him a "sausage" - but even that did not last long.Within minutes, Fury was offering to go for a pint with the Matchroom boss - and extended the invitation to Joshua."I hope after this fight we can have a pint of Guinness together," Fury said. "Win, lose or draw, let's bury the hatchet.""I don't know if I can trust you," Joshua replied, drawing laughter.The overriding mood was one of relief between two veterans, who were seemingly happy to let the fight settle what years of talk could not.

schema.headline: Fury vs Joshua: Heavyweights trade jokes at launch event

title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest
description: The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made
body: The winning entry of a prestigious scientific photography competition is being re-evaluated following criticism from other scientists that it was made with AI.Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest accepts photos and video taken using powerful microscopes, and has run annually for the last 15 years.The winner was a short video submitted by Dr Ning Xu, a researcher at Tsinghua University in China, which claims to be footage of tiny, hair-like structures called cilia moving inside the airways of a child with a rare disease.Xu did not respond to the BBC's request for comment, but has posted online denying he broke the competition rules.In a response to a post by Nikon on LinkedIn, external, he did not dispute using AI within the image processing but said he remained within the rules of the contest."AI was not used to generate the experimental movie, the cilia, or their motion," he said. Xu's video is artificially brightly coloured - common in microscopy and permitted in the contest - which is usually done manually using stains and dyes on the sample itself.He accepted AI was used "to distinguish and visualize features in the reconstructed grayscale images".But the challenges made by other scientists include claims that the video contains shapes and movements which did not fit with normal cell structures or behaviours, and that the cilia seemed to be too big.Commenting on Nikon's social media post, Edward Phelps, associate professor at Florida University, observed some of the structures "pop in and out of existence" and the cilia "appear from nowhere".Meanwhile PhD student Ian Donovan from UT Southwestern Medical Centre said the source image appeared to contain a distinctive watermark indicating it had been AI generated.Additionally, two former competition judges said they also had concerns about whether the image was real.Nikon said Xu was "respectfully complying" with its investigation and had provided it with additional technical documents.Dr Patrick Hickey, who came fifth in the 2026 Small World contest, said the recognition the award represents means more than the $3,000 (£2,250) prize itself."If you spend a lot of your time in a dark room looking down a microscope, it's really nice to be able to show people and to show the public," he said."There's an interesting fusion between science and art, and a lot of the images that scientists are making have some very abstract and artistic qualities to them."Hickey said it would be unfair on other entrants if it turned out the winning video was unfairly altered by AI."There's a specific set of rules in the contest, and one of them was quite clearly that you couldn't use generative AI to produce things, and the other was obviously that it has to be taken under a microscope," he said.So far, Nikon is standing by its procedures but it said there would be an update soon."At this time, we don't see that any rules were violated," it said in a statement.

schema.headline: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest

title: Conservatives pledge 'tough love' benefit rules for under-25s
description: The Conservatives have said they would introduce new work requirements for under-25s claiming benefits in a "tough love" approach to youth joblessness
body: The Conservatives have said they would introduce new work requirements for under-25s claiming benefits in a "tough love" approach to youth joblessness.Young people claiming Universal Credit who are fit to work but have not worked for six months continuously would face new rules to qualify for payments, including daily attendance at a job centre or courses.The party says the scheme would help tackle the almost one million people aged 16 to 24 in the UK who are not in education, employment or training, known as Neets.But anti-poverty charity Trussell warned that people on Universal Credit could not afford basic essentials, which harmed their ability to find and keep work.Under the Tory proposals, those aged 18 to 24 who apply for Universal Credit but have not previously worked for a continuous period of six months or more, for at least 16 hours per week, would instead have to take part in a "Get to Work" scheme.Rather than Universal Credit, they would receive a "Get to Work Allowance" paid at the same rate but requiring daily attendance at a job centre, on work experience or work readiness courses.They would be assigned a manager and have to take part in job search workshops and interview preparation sessions.The programme would last six months, or less if a participant secures a job - but those who are still unemployed after half a year on the scheme would have their benefit cut by 30%.Young people on Universal Credit who have previously worked for six months, have health issues or care responsibilities or are estranged would be exempt.The party has also said it would look closer at whether parents' earnings and savings should be factored into welfare payments for their children.Shadow work and pensions secretary Helen Whately said the measures were designed to "show some tough love" to reduce the number of Neets."Too many young people are leaving school and signing straight onto benefits - this is a waste of their potential and a disaster for our economy," the Tory MP said.

schema.headline: Conservatives pledge 'tough love' benefit rules for under-25s
